script: doc/scripts/cost_measure.py (experiments stages, threads, panel, grid, disp, sim, example, cad, plots); figures: doc/scripts/make_plots.py (cost_stages, cost_threads, cost_scaling), doc/figures/tikz/cost_estimate_flow.tex

measured_here.machine: Intel Core i7-12700 (8 P cores + 4 E cores, 20 threads), 30 GB, Linux 7.0
measured_here.binary: target/release/ignisyeet of commit 2a345c2 (release/v0.4.0), cargo build --release -p ignisyeet
measured_here.method: /usr/bin/time -f '%e %U %S %M' around ignisyeet --no-progress <subcommand> ... --set resources.threads=N; 3 repeats, median (min and max kept); cpu = user + system; rss = largest peak RSS; load = /proc/loadavg (1 min) before each run
measured_here.load: The machine was shared with SU2 jobs of other work (about 15 to 20 MPI ranks); the 1-minute load average was 1 to 54 during the runs and is recorded per row (column load). No dedicated machine was available. The thread-scaling run and the dispersion size sweep were done twice, once in a quiet period (threads_quiet.csv, load 2 to 13; dispersion_scaling_quiet.csv, load 7 to 27) and once while the machine was busy (threads.csv, load 18 to 41; dispersion_scaling.csv, load 17 to 25); all other files were measured while it was busy (load 17 to 41). Wall times are inflated by 1.5 to 3 times against an idle machine, CPU times by less.

files.stages.csv: stage times at 4 threads (geom, aero barrowman / panel / cached, sim rk4 / rk45 / dop853, dispersion grid and Monte Carlo, report), load 21 to 26
files.threads.csv: busy-machine run: panel table, wind grid (224 flights, rk4) and Monte Carlo (4000 flights, rk45) at 1, 2, 4, 8 and 20 threads (load average 18 to 41)
files.panel_mesh.csv: panel table time and memory against the panel mesh at 4 threads; subsonic_s = the program's own time of the six subsonic solves
files.table_grid.csv: Barrowman table time and file size against the Mach x alpha grid; last row: table_kind = general
files.dispersion_scaling.csv: wind grid and Monte Carlo time, memory and output size against the number of flights (rk45, 4 threads); last two rows: rk4 and dop853 with 112 flights
files.sim_cost.csv: one flight against integrator, dt, output_interval and earth.model (flat / ecef)
files.example_run.csv: panel table, 36 x 6 wind grid and 10^4 Monte Carlo samples in a row (the worked estimate of the chapter)
files.cad_mesh.csv: geom from the STEP file (cold and cached tessellation) and cfd-check --mesh (gmsh, one thread) for sample_cfd.toml and sample_step.toml, one run each, on a copy of the example files in the scratch directory (second run, load 16-20; an earlier run at load 43-54 gave 118 s and 355 s for the two meshes and was overwritten)
files.plots.csv: python/plot.py (doc/.venv interpreter) on the result files of one run
files.threads_quiet.csv: the same experiment in a quiet period (load average 2 to 13; the 8-thread Monte Carlo row has a wide range because the load rose during it)
files.dispersion_scaling_quiet.csv: the same sweep as dispersion_scaling.csv in a quieter period (load average 7 to 27)

measured_here.not_done: The virgo cluster was not used; no dedicated or idle machine was measured.

quoted.cfd_quoted.csv: CFD times and cells quoted from doc/data/cfd/run_summary.json (Euler, 16 cases: total_wall_s 9149, mesh_s 25), doc/data/cfd/sample_euler_cases.csv (case wall_seconds), doc/data/cfd/rans_table_run.json (run_wall_h 4.4404), doc/data/cfd/rans_table_cases.csv, doc/data/cfd/rans_mesh_sweep.csv; SU2 was not run for this chapter
quoted.threads_quoted.csv: thread scaling quoted from doc/data/perf/profile_2026-10-08.md (commit b6a9bf5, load average 12-15); the 20-thread panel time of the retired timing table of the validation chapter (8.1-9.7 s) is not used because it came from another run than the 1-thread time
not_in_csv: CFD memory and per-case numbers of the mesh convergence runs: doc/data/cfd/mesh_convergence.csv, rans_memory.csv, resource_plan.csv, rans_mesh_sweep.csv
CFD workdir disk of one Euler run (mesh 72 MB, 52 MB per case): du of an existing run of sample_cfd.toml (1415504 cells), not committed

SU2 native versus conda-forge ratios and the speed-up table of the STL / rebuilt-geometry comparison: moved from the validation chapter (doc/data/cfd/su2_native_benchmark.csv, stl_cross_check_runs.json)
panel time at low load (11.3 s, 8 threads, load 2-4): doc/data/panel/mesh_cost.csv

corrections: The retired timing table of the validation chapter gave 3818 s for the 16 Euler cases while its text and doc/data/cfd/run_summary.json give 9149 s (sum of the case times 9118 s plus 25 s of meshing); 9149 s is used, and doc/data/perf/profile_2026-10-08.md was corrected (Euler rows).
The profile of 2026-10-08 counted about 110 supersonic columns of the panel table; with Mach 1.2 to 3.0 in steps of 0.02 there are 91.
